challenges.name: iterator-invalidation-quiz
challenges.title: Predict it: erase loops and stale iterators
challenges.description: Run an erase loop in your head, then decide which operations leave a saved iterator pointing at nothing.

questions.explanation: Step through it. i = 0: 45 is below 50 and is erased, everything moves one slot left ({30, 75, 20, 15, 90}), then ++i makes i = 1 - so 30, which now sits in slot 0, is never checked. i = 1: 75 stays. i = 2: 20 is erased ({30, 75, 15, 90}) and 15 slides into slot 2, which is skipped by ++i. i = 3: 90 stays, and i = 4 ends the loop. The result is 30 75 15 90: two results below 50 survive, each one right after an erased element. "75 90" is what the loop was meant to do. "30 75 90" and "75 15 90" each skip only one of the two survivors. The behaviour is not undefined: i is compared with the current size() on every pass, so every access is in range - the program is wrong, but deterministically wrong, which is exactly why it passed review.

options.text: The behaviour is undefined: it may print anything or crash

questions.explanation: push_back on a full vector (size == capacity) must allocate a bigger buffer, move the elements there and free the old one, so every iterator, pointer and reference into the vector is invalidated - _GLIBCXX_DEBUG reports "attempt to dereference a singular iterator" when first is used. erase(roster.begin()) invalidates the erased position and everything after it, and first IS the erased position. reserve(100) asks for more capacity than the vector has, which also reallocates and invalidates everything. pop_back() only invalidates the last element and end(); first, at position 0, stays valid and still refers to the first student. A std::map never moves its elements: insert invalidates no iterator, so found still refers to RP-2024-0101 (erase would invalidate only the erased element).

challenges.name: fix-roster-cleanup
challenges.title: Fix the roster clean-up that skips students
challenges.description: Before every exam, clean_roster() removes withdrawn students and repeated rows from a class roster, and returns how many rows it removed. The code was ported from the 2010 C tool and uses index loops with erase. When two withdrawn students are next to each other, one of them stays on the exam list, and when a student appears three times in a row, one duplicate stays. Fix clean_roster() so that every withdrawn row is removed, then only the first row for each student id is kept, the order of the rest is unchanged, and the count is right. The test runner reads the roster, calls clean_roster() once and prints the count and the exam list.
